disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to make an appropriate referral to a qualified health care provider for a condition that should be referred

disciplinary_grounds.description: Designating a hearing instrument for a patient whose hearing will not be sufficiently improved to justify prescribing and selling it

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making false, misleading, deceptive, fraudulent, or exaggerated claims about practice or hearing instrument benefits

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to exercise caution in providing a prognosis so the patient is not led to expect unpredictable results
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failing to exercise caution in providing a patient a prognosis to assure the patient is not led to expect results that cannot be accurately predicted

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to provide appropriate follow-up care when a patient reports the hearing instrument does not produce represented results
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failing to provide appropriate follow-up care and consultation with respect to a patient to whom a hearing instrument has been prescribed and sold upon being informed by the patient that the hearing instrument does not produce the results represented by the licensee

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to disclose in writing the charge for all services and hearing instruments prior to providing them
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failing to disclose in writing to the patient the charge for all services and hearing instruments prescribed and sold to a patient prior to providing the services or hearing instrument

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to refund fees when the division determines the patient has not obtained the represented hearing recovery

definition_quote.value: "Practice of a hearing instrument specialist" means: (a) establishing a place of business to practice as a hearing instrument specialist; (b) testing the hearing of a human patient over the age of 17 for the sole purpose of determining whether a hearing loss will be sufficiently improved by the use of a hearing instrument to justify prescribing and selling the hearing instrument and whether that hearing instrument will be in the best interest of the patient; (c) providing the patient a written statement of prognosis regarding the need for or usefulness of a hearing instrument for the patient's condition; (d) prescribing an appropriate hearing instrument; (e) making impressions or earmolds for the fitting of a hearing instrument; (f) sale and professional placement of the hearing instrument on a patient; (g) evaluating the hearing loss overcome by the installation of the hearing instrument and evaluating the hearing recovery against the representations made to the patient by the hearing instrument specialist; (h) necessary intervention to produce satisfactory hearing recovery results from a hearing instrument; or (i) instructing the patient on the use and care of the hearing instrument.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of a hearing instrument specialist" means: (a) establishing a place of business to practice as a hearing instrument specialist; (b) testing the hearing of a human patient over the age of 17
